_note: Template colours. Primary, Secondary and (cockpit) Neon come from the native build paint in scripts/vehicle_blockouts/specs/exotic.json. The game repaints Primary, Secondary, Detail, Neon and ThrustColor parts at spawn and in previews, so template colours on those channels only matter when a template is viewed raw in Studio. Glass and lamp colours are final: no script touches them.
_finish: 2026-10-04, Oscar: match the look of Workspace ExoticMeshPilot_WIP. Reflectance per part channel (primary, secondary, glass), glass at 0.15 transparency and Plastic detail parts. No game script writes Reflectance or these materials, so the template values carry into Play.
_meshLamp: mesh/INTEGRATION.md D10. Mesh modules (kits 02 and 05) do not use the kit neon for lamps: the lights channel is always this white and the lights_red channel always this red. Both go in LIGHTS_AlwaysOn with PaintChannel Lights.
_lamp: kitNeon = the native neon paint of the cockpit that owns the kit (as the blockout shows it). A hex value here gives every Nose and Engine Deck lamp that colour instead.
_defaultLights: DefaultFrontLightsColor and DefaultRearLightsColor are the values every Piercer cockpit carries. Exotic cockpits have no Neon-channel parts, so only the paint UI reads them.
_glass: Pilot Play test 2026-10-03: the blockout glass (#5f8fb0 at 0.35) read milky white under the garage lights. Dark tint, as the concept art and the Piercer canopy.
